meaning: Control cannot read the outdoor sensor due to a short circuit. It assumes an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continues operation. Clear after repair by pressing the Item button.
causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.
Very high resistance: broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor. Very low resistance: shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or defective sensor.
Measure directly at the sensor location to isolate the sensor from the wiring.

meaning: Control could not read a piece of information from its EEPROM. It loads factory defaults and stops operation until all settings are verified.
checks: Verify all settings in the Adjust menu.
Check the quality of the 24 V power supply.

meaning: Control failed to read the boiler supply sensor due to a short circuit. With a call for heat it no longer controls the boiler(s); it provides a boiler enable to the boiler aquastat or control until repaired. It will not operate the boiler contact if Boil Minimum is below 100 F (38 C). Self clears when corrected.
causes: Short circuit in the sensor wiring
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then measure the sensor resistance and compare with the resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F.

meaning: Control failed to read the boiler supply sensor due to an open circuit. It no longer controls the boiler; it provides a boiler enable to the boiler aquastat or control until repaired. It will not operate the boiler contact if Boil Minimum is below 100 F (38 C). Self clears when corrected.
checks: Disconnect the sensor wires from the control before testing; never apply voltage to a sensor.

If the supply sensor was removed deliberately, power the control down for 10 seconds, then restart it.

meaning: Communication lost on the Boiler Bus due to a short or open circuit.
causes: Short or open circuit on the tN4 bus
checks: Check the tN4, C and R wires for each tN4 device.
Check the polarity of the C and R wires.
Check for loose or broken wires.

meaning: Control failed to read the Adjust Menu settings and reloaded factory defaults. Operation stops until all Adjust Menu settings are checked.
checks: Set the access level to Advanced and check all settings in the Adjust menu to clear the error.

meaning: More than one tN4 device has been assigned the same master number.
causes: Duplicate schedule master number on the network
checks: Reassign master numbers so each tN4 device has a unique one.
